title: Bottom-row cohomology descent by finite hypercover refinements
statement: For X qcqs, R any ring, a sheaf F of R-modules, a nonnegative injective resolution I of F [def-sp-injective-resolutions] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], a finite split etale hypercover U [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover], and q in N, use the explicit total bicomplex and bottom inclusion b_U:C(U,F) to Tot D(U,I) [lem-sc-hypercover-resolution-comparison]. Every class y in H^q(Tot D(U,I)) restricts along some finite split refinement f:V to U to a class b_V(x) with x in H^q(C(V,F)). Every x in H^q(C(U,F)) with b_U(x)=0 becomes zero after some finite split refinement. These assertions concern the actual chain maps; they do not assert the natural comparison or its colimit universal property.

source.place: Tag 01H0, theorem-cohomology-hypercoverings, first proof using an injective-resolution double complex.

proof.text: Represent a total q-class by a cocycle. Starting at its largest positive resolution degree, the total-cycle equation gives a vertical cycle in the corresponding exact resolution short complex. Obtain a vertical primitive on the whole corresponding refined term.

Work with resolution degree first. Induct on the largest supported positive resolution degree. Include the chosen primitive into total degree q-1 and subtract its total differential; explicit total projections show the top component is killed and support decreases. Compose refinements and add the transported corrections. At resolution degree zero, evaluation preserves the resolution kernel, so lift uniquely to F; monicity of F to I0 gives the horizontal cocycle equation. Quotient by boundaries to obtain the representative. The signed total-flip isomorphism identifies this calculation with the comparison model; its sign is one on the bottom row, and its naturality transports all refinement maps.

For a bottom class mapping to zero, choose a bounding total (q-1)-cochain. Its differential lies entirely in the bottom row. Run the same corrections above that row, again using whole-term vertical primitives. The corrected bound lifts to a cochain of F whose differential is the refined original cocycle. For q=0 there is no negative term; injectivity of F to I0 makes the original cocycle zero. Only degrees through q+1 are used.

lean.statement:
theorem bottom_refinement_descent {X : Scheme.{u}} [CompactSpace X]
    [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (R : Type (u + 1)) [Ring R]
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R)) (I : InjectiveResolution F)
    (U : FiniteSplitEtaleHypercover X) (q : ℕ) :
    (∀ y : ((resolutionDoubleComplex R U I.cocomplex).total (.up ℕ)).homology q,
      ∃ (V : FiniteSplitEtaleHypercover X) (f : V.Refinement U)
        (x : ((sectionComplexFunctor R V).obj F).homology q),
      HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (bottomInclusion R V I) q x =
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (totalRefinement R f I.cocomplex) q y) ∧
    (∀ x : ((sectionComplexFunctor R U).obj F).homology q,
      HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (bottomInclusion R U I) q x = 0 →
      ∃ (V : FiniteSplitEtaleHypercover X) (f : V.Refinement U),
        (cohomologyRefinement (ModuleCat R) f q).app F x = 0)
